idiom_name: reusable double object with a test-only configuration interface (or record/playback mode)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: implement the depended-on component's interface in a test-only type whose fields hold the values to return and the arguments to expect, and expose those fields through a configuration interface that only the test uses - per-value setters, constructor parameters, or a fluent expectation builder. Configure the double during fixture setup, install it through a substitutable-dependency seam, and let the system under test see only the production interface; re-create or reset the double for each test so configured state cannot leak. Where the language or its ecosystem offers a mocking toolkit, that toolkit plays the roles of generator and configuration interface; where it does not, exactly this structure is hand-written.
code_sketch:
double = configurable_double.of(Collaborator)
double.configure(returns={"now": instant, "charge": [ok, timeout]})   # fixture setup
double.expects("charge", args=(amount, currency))                    # expectations
sut = SystemUnderTest(double)                                          # install
sut.run()                                                              # exercise
assert double.verify()                                                 # verify
pitfalls: Configuring a double that is never reset or re-created, so responses and recorded calls leak between tests.
Letting the configuration interface bleed into production-facing types or into a test mode the production code can enter.
Replacing the part of the system that is supposed to be under test, so the test verifies the double instead of the software.
Overspecifying expectations on call arguments, causing tests to break on refactoring that does not change behaviour.
Using an unspec'd dynamic double that accepts calls to methods which no longer exist on the real collaborator.
Configuring impossible return values - values the real collaborator could never produce - and treating a green test as evidence of correct production behaviour.
Temporal coupling: configuring a double to expect calls in a specific order that does not matter to the behaviour under test.
Forgetting to await async mock returns in async tests, causing the test to pass prematurely before the operation completes.
Using a synchronous mock for an async method without properly configuring it as awaitable (e.g., ReturnsAsync in Moq, AsyncMock in unittest.mock).
Configuring nested mocks (a double that returns another double) without limiting depth, producing opaque failure messages.

Wrong move: stubbing every collaborator method 'just in case' -> tests pass on their own configuration while production paths go unexercised and any interface change breaks dozens of tests -> instead configure only what the test depends on and run in strict/specced mode (Mockito strictness, unittest.mock autospec) so unused or unknown stubs fail loudly.

Wrong move: configuring doubles directly against third-party library classes -> a library upgrade changes internal call sequences and unrelated tests break -> instead wrap the dependency in an adapter you own and configure the double against the adapter's interface.

Wrong move: mocking your own simple value types or stable framework contracts to save fixture-setup effort -> the double cannot uphold the API's real guarantees and tests drift from reality -> instead use the real instance or assert on observable outcomes, reserving configurable doubles for slow, nondeterministic or side-effecting collaborators.
